commits.message:
fix(parsing): stop truncating job descriptions and misclassifying postings as resumes

Bug report: "the parsing is not properly done and only partial
information is parsed... especially for emails from
phph001@prohirespowerhouse.com. all the emails are parsing the same
style, only partial data is parsed though the text is proper in the
raw data." Confirmed: 100% of drafts sourced from this sender had
job_description == "Remove/" -- every real field the posting actually
contained (skills, location, duration, rate, responsibilities) was
gone.

Root cause: this vendor's broadcast platform puts its unsubscribe/
manage-subscription masthead at the very TOP of the email, right after
the From:/Subject: header block -- "Remove/unsubscribe | Update your
contact and subscribed mailing list(s) | Subscribe to mailing list(s)
to receive requirements & resumes". _JOB_DESCRIPTION_FOOTER_MARKERS'
"unsubscribe" marker (app/email_parsing/parsers.py) assumes an
unsubscribe mention sits near the END of the text -- a real footer --
and cuts everything from its FIRST occurrence onward. With this
vendor's masthead at the top instead, that cut landed seven characters
in: "Remove/" is everything before "unsubscribe" in "Remove/
unsubscribe". Fixed by recognizing this masthead line as top-of-email
preamble (same treatment _strip_forwarded_header_block already gives
the jobs.nvoids.com relay preamble and security-gateway banners), so
it's stripped before the footer-cut logic ever sees it.

Investigated the specific message ID the user also pointed at
(khushank@sourceinfotech.com via the jobs.nvoids.com relay) and found a
second, related bug with the same "partial parsing" symptom but a
different mechanism: that email got document_kind="resume" instead of
"job_description", which skips the structured job-requirement parser
entirely (email_parsing.records stays empty, confidence 0.0, wrong
draft_type). Cause: jobs.nvoids.com appends "Free resume and job search
portal" to the footer of literally every posting it relays, including
pure requirements with zero resume content -- and
app/channels/service.py:detect_document_kind's keyword-marker fallback
(used whenever recipient-address routing and both parsers' own
structural confidence are inconclusive) scanned the RAW, unstripped
text, so that one boilerplate word was enough to misclassify a genuine
job posting. Same fix pattern: strip known job-board-relay boilerplate
(now exposed as a public strip_job_board_boilerplate wrapper in
parsers.py, reusing the same header/footer stripping
_clean_job_description already does) before the fallback classifier
ever sees the text.

Also broadened detect_document_kind's jd_markers with "mandatory
skills" / "duration:" / "interview process" -- phrasing several real
vendors use instead of "required skills"/"rate"/"location", which
previously fell through the classifier entirely (landing on
"plain_message", same failure mode of skipping structured parsing).

New coverage: scripts/hermes-850-email-parsing-check.py gets a
regression test reproducing the exact prohirespowerhouse email and
asserting the description survives intact and the masthead line itself
is still stripped; scripts/hermes-850-self-learning-classification-
check.py gets two tests -- the exact nvoids/sourceinfotech email no
longer misclassifies as a resume, and "Mandatory Skills" phrasing is
recognized as a job posting. Full regression suite run against a fresh
schema and freshly built image: every touched script passes, including
the 3 new checks; every other failure in the suite reproduces
identically against the current, unmodified production image in the
same throwaway harness (missing live server, missing Langfuse/MS Graph
credentials) -- confirmed pre-existing environment gaps, not
regressions from this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
